description: How the apps name a playback failure: from the HTTP status of the server's answer (null: no answer at all) and its text (the plain-text body, an offer's `reasons` joined with "; ", or a file's `broken_reason`), and `pending` (an offer still indexing), the kind of problem. Each kind has a short title and one plain line in every app; the server's own text stays available as the details. Rules, first match wins: no answer -> unreachable; pending -> preparing; then by the text (case-insensitive): "no such file or directory" -> missing; "can't be reached", "not mounted", "isn't mounted" -> share; "damaged", "incomplete", "truncated", "ebml", "invalid data found", "moov atom not found", "end of file" -> damaged; "keyframe index pending" -> preparing; "keyframe index", "no cues" -> unindexed; "slots busy" -> busy; then 404 (the title has no file the server can find) -> missing; 500 and above -> server; anything else -> unsupported. Checked by the Apple apps (PlaybackProblemTests), the Android apps (PlaybackProblemCasesTest) and the Windows app (SharedCasesTests).
